title: Reproducibility of Pollution–Health Evidence Synthesis Using LLM-Assisted Screening and Extraction — code, data, prompts, and raw outputs (companion to Research Synthesis Methods submission)
description:
This deposit accompanies the manuscript “Reproducibility of Pollution–Health Evidence Synthesis Using LLM-Assisted Screening and Extraction” submitted to Research Synthesis Methods (Cambridge University Press).

Contents:

  • 500-abstract corpus (PubMed search Feb 2026; PM2.5 × respiratory hospitalization)
  • Heuristic gold standard (screening + extraction templates)
  • Stratified subset of 100 abstracts for dual-human labeling
  • Exact prompts for screening + extraction (variable-length and fixed-slot variants)
  • JSON Schemas for output validation
  • Raw outputs from 6 models × 10 runs × 2 stages = 36,000 LLM calls
  • Cloud-deployment desconfound experiment: meta-llama/llama-3-8b-instruct via OpenRouter:DeepInfra (10 runs)
  • Silver-external gold standard: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model (5 runs, 100 items)
  • Fixed-slot extraction sensitivity: Claude/Gemini/GPT-4.1 (3 runs each)
  • Complete analysis scripts (16 files) with no SDK dependencies
  • Provenance hashing (SHA-256 call_hash + output_hash)
  • Run cards with timestamps, durations, token counts

Reproducibility statement: all numerical results, tables, and figures in the manuscript derive deterministically from the deposited raw outputs via the included scripts. The requirements-lock.txt pins exact dependency versions used during the experiments (Python 3.14.3 on macOS Darwin 24.6.0, Apple M4 silicon).

License: code under MIT; data and prompts under CC-BY-4.0.

Companion paper: Rover & Tadano (2026), “Hidden Non-Determinism in Large Language Model APIs: A Lightweight Provenance Protocol for Reproducible Generative AI Research” (JAIR, in press).
